faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.missing: Can't find your question? <contactLink>Write to us</contactLink>, we reply within 48 hours and add it here.

cost.question: How much does a 6 kWp installation cost?
cost.answer: The price depends on the roof, the inverter and the options (battery, backup). We do not publish a price list: every quote is fixed, itemised line by line and issued after a free study. The simulator first gives you the expected production and savings.

financing.question: Can I finance my installation?
financing.answer: Yes, with our partner Sofinco for individuals, or through leasing with BPCE Lease for businesses.

deposit.question: What deposit is due at signature?
deposit.answer: The deposit amount and the payment schedule are set out in the fixed, itemised quote before anything is signed. [Amount and schedule to be confirmed by Soliance]

payback.question: How many years until the installation pays for itself?
payback.answer: It depends on your consumption, the share you consume yourself and the battery size: the study works out this period for your home before the quote. A real example: the villa in Vence (16 kWp, 15 kWh) shows a payback of 7.5 years.

maintenance.question: Is maintenance included?
maintenance.answer: Yes, for the first year. After that, Soliance Care takes over: 24/7 monitoring, annual servicing and repairs within 2 working days, from €19.99/month.

solarBonus.question: Is there still a grant for solar panels?
solarBonus.answer: No self-consumption bonus is active at the moment. We do not include it in our quotes; if it is reinstated, it will be deducted at signature.

resale.question: Can I still sell my electricity?
resale.answer: Total sale is no longer available to individuals and surplus is bought back at €0.01 per kWh, 20 times less than the price you pay for it. That is why all our residential installations include a battery.

maPrimeRenov.question: Does MaPrimeRénov' apply to solar panels?
maPrimeRenov.answer: No. MaPrimeRénov' and CEE do not cover photovoltaics: they apply to heat pumps. We check your eligibility during the study and file the applications.

vatRecovery.question: Can I recover the VAT?
vatRecovery.answer: Yes, on request, for installations over 3 kWp: we set up the producer structure and handle the file until the refund.

chargerAids.question: What incentives are there for an EV charger?
chargerAids.answer: A tax credit for a smart charger installed by an IRVE-qualified installer, reduced VAT in homes over 2 years old, and the Advenir programme for condominiums and businesses.

roof.question: Is my roof suitable?
roof.answer: South, south-east or south-west facing, 15 to 45° pitch, tiles, slate or steel sheet: we check on satellite view, then during a technical visit.

battery.question: Why a battery on every installation?
battery.answer: With surplus bought back at €0.01 per kWh, every kilowatt-hour you do not use is lost. The battery keeps the daytime production for the evening and night: 70 to 85% self-sufficiency depending on the household.

hardware.question: What equipment do you install?
hardware.answer: Francilienne 450 to 500 W panels, Solax IES hybrid inverters, T30 / T58 batteries, an EPS box for backup power and K2 mounting systems. For heat pumps, mainly Daikin.

outage.question: What happens during a power cut?
outage.answer: With the EPS box, the battery keeps powering the essentials of the house while the grid is down.

heatPumpCoupling.question: Can I pair a heat pump with my solar panels?
heatPumpCoupling.answer: Yes, and it is the ideal pair: the heat pump and the heat-pump water heater use your daytime solar production.

connection.question: How long until I am connected?
connection.answer: About 10 days from first contact to signature, then 1 to 3 months of paperwork (town hall, Enedis) before installation.

paperwork.question: What paperwork do I have to do myself?
paperwork.answer: None: the town hall declaration, the Enedis connection, the Consuel and the buy-back contract are all handled by Soliance.

installationDays.question: How many days does installation take?
installationDays.answer: 1 to 3 days for solar depending on the power, 1 to 2 days for a heat pump, half a day to a day for a charger. Always by our own technicians.

heatPumpLeadTime.question: How long does it take to install a heat pump?
heatPumpLeadTime.answer: About 10 days from first contact to signature, then 3 to 6 weeks depending on the grants to obtain before work starts. No town hall or Enedis paperwork.

chargerLeadTime.question: And for an EV charger?
chargerLeadTime.answer: Quote within 48 hours of the visit, installation within 2 to 3 weeks, in half a day to a day. No town hall paperwork.

breakdown.question: What happens if something breaks down?
breakdown.answer: The first year of maintenance is included. After that, Soliance Care monitors the installation and steps in within 2 working days.

coverage.question: Which warranties cover my installation?
coverage.answer: Soliance's ten-year liability insurance, with MMA, and the manufacturer warranties on the equipment, including a 25-year product warranty on Francilienne panels.

manufacturerWarranty.question: Who handles manufacturer warranties?
manufacturerWarranty.answer: We do, directly: we have installed and repaired the same brands since 2022, and we handle manufacturer warranties ourselves if there is a problem.

installer.question: Who installs the system?
installer.answer: Our own technicians, based in Saint-Laurent-du-Var. We do not subcontract installation.

heatPumpServicing.question: What servicing does a heat pump need?
heatPumpServicing.answer: An annual check is mandatory above 4 kW. It is included the first year, then offered with Soliance Care.

reward.question: How much does a referral earn?
reward.answer: €300 for the 1st referee, €400 for the 2nd, €500 for the 3rd, €600 for the 4th, then a weekend for two at the 5th. No time limit.

eligibility.question: Who can refer someone?
eligibility.answer: Soliance and Soliance Care customers. The referee must not already be in contact with Soliance.

payment.question: When is the reward paid?
payment.answer: By bank transfer, within 30 days of the referee's installation being commissioned.

installations.question: Which installations count?
installations.answer: Solar, heat pump or charger: every installation counts.

howTo.question: How do I pass on a contact?
howTo.answer: Through the form on the Referral page, by phone on 06 08 62 84 71 or from your customer area, with your referee's consent.

glossary.title: Incentives and programmes glossary
glossary.updated: Updated on [date] · amounts checked every quarter

selfConsumptionBonus.definition: A government grant that existed for self-consumption installations. No bonus is active at the moment: we do not include it in our quotes. If it is reinstated, it will be deducted at signature.

feedInTariff.definition: The contract under which EDF buys unused surplus. For individuals, the rate is €0.01 per kWh and total sale is no longer offered: hence a battery on all our installations and smart-controlled equipment (water heater, charger).

vatRecovery.definition: For an installation over 3 kWp, individuals can recover the VAT by becoming a VAT-registered producer. Soliance sets up the structure and prepares the file.

maPrimeRenov.definition: An Anah grant for replacing a heating system with a heat pump, based on income. Does not cover solar. Application prepared by Soliance.

energySavingsCertificates.definition: A bonus funded by energy suppliers, combinable with MaPrimeRénov' for a heat pump. Paid after the work by an RGE installer.

consuel.definition: The electrical compliance certificate required before grid connection. Requested and obtained by Soliance for every installation.

gridConnection.definition: Planning permission from the town hall, then a grid connection request. Allow 1 to 3 months, included in the quote.

certifications.definition: Labels required for customers to receive incentives. Soliance holds the QualiPV and QualiPac qualifications.

aperLaw.definition: An obligation to add solar to car parks over 1,500 m²; the option to share production among several consumers in the same neighbourhood.

decennialWarranty.definition: The installer's mandatory insurance: for 10 years after the work is accepted, it covers damage that undermines the installation's soundness or makes it unfit for use. Soliance holds ten-year cover with MMA.

performanceWarranty.definition: The manufacturer's commitment on the output the panels retain over the years. It comes on top of the product warranty, 25 years on the Francilienne panels we install.

chargingInfrastructure.definition: Electric vehicle charging infrastructure. The IRVE qualification is mandatory to install a charger above 3.7 kW and to qualify for incentives: our electricians are IRVE-qualified.

powerAndEnergy.definition: The kWp (kilowatt-peak) measures the panels' maximum power, the kWh the energy produced or consumed. Our estimates use ≈ 1,300 kWh per kWp per year in the region.

hybridInverter.definition: It converts the panels' direct current into alternating current for the home and manages battery charging and discharging. We install Solax IES hybrid inverters.

backupBox.definition: A backup power unit: during a grid outage, the battery keeps powering the essentials of the house.

selfConsumption.definition: Using the electricity your panels produce on site. With a battery, self-sufficiency reaches 70 to 85% depending on the household: that is why all our residential installations include one.

surplus.definition: Electricity produced but neither used nor stored, fed into the grid and bought back at €0.01 per kWh, 20 times less than its purchase price. We size every installation to keep it low.

care.definition: Our monitoring and maintenance service: 24/7 monitoring, annual servicing and repairs within 2 working days by a local technician. From €19.99/month.

referral.definition: Our recommendation programme: €300 to €600 per referee depending on their rank, and a weekend for two at the 5th, paid after their installation is commissioned.
